title: LightOnOCR-3
idiom: 16th-century woodcut scriptorium, red ink boxes drawn round each block of a pinned page, one crumpled page still unread
hero_prompt: Sixteenth-century woodcut illustration, black ink on warm cream paper with a single accent of vermilion red, hand-cut wood texture, bold carved lines and cross-hatching, flat and graphic, not a photograph, not a 3D render, wide panoramic composition: a scribe in a plain cap stands at a tall slanted lectern, quill raised, copying a large printed sheet pinned to a board beside him onto a fresh blank sheet; on the pinned sheet every block of print — a heading band, two columns of text, a small ruled grid of a table — has a neat rectangle drawn round it in red ink, like a surveyor's plot; the copy on his lectern repeats the same blocks in the same places; at the foot of the board, half off the edge, a crumpled, torn, rain-stained page lies unread with no red box around it. The print is rendered only as rows of tiny abstract marks.
icon_prompt: Linocut emblem, a flat single-colour black silhouette on a vermilion-red ground, no shading or gradients: a round reading lens held over a small rectangle of four ruled lines, with four bold corner brackets framing the rectangle. Bold, high-contrast, no fine linework, reads clearly at 24 pixels.
